verdict: Disney's revenue rose 5% to $26.0B and its parks set a record — but Entertainment profit fell 35% on higher programming and marketing costs, pulling total segment profit down 9%.

segments.name: Services
segments.note: Streaming subscriptions, TV networks and channels, park tickets and hotel stays — the large majority of Disney's money.

segments.name: Products
segments.note: Merchandise, food and drinks, and other things Disney physically sells.

opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Marketing the movies, shows and parks, and running the company.

opex.name: Depreciation & amortization
opex.note: The wear and tear on parks, cruise ships and equipment, spread over their working lives.

follow100Note: Of the $9.56 kept as profit per $100 of revenue, about $0.32 belongs to noncontrolling partners — $9.25 is Disney shareholders'. Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.

takeaways.title: A record quarter at the parks
takeaways.text: Revenue rose 5% to $26.0B. Experiences — parks, resorts and cruises — set a record with $10.0B of revenue, and Entertainment revenue grew 7% on a big theatrical slate (Zootopia 2, Avatar: Fire and Ash) and higher streaming rates.

takeaways.title: Parks are the profit engine
takeaways.text: Experiences operating income rose 6% to $3.3B — three times Entertainment's — as domestic park profit grew 8% on 1% higher attendance and 4% higher spending per guest.

takeaways.title: Entertainment profit shrank
takeaways.text: Entertainment operating income fell 35% to $1.1B: higher programming, production and marketing costs for the quarter's big releases outweighed the extra revenue. Sports profit also fell, partly on a temporary YouTube TV carriage suspension.

oneTimers: The temporary suspension of YouTube TV carriage cost the Sports segment about $110M of operating income in the quarter.
There were no restructuring and impairment charges this quarter (a year ago there were $143M).
otherDetail: Interest expense, net, of $275M on Disney's debt, partly offset by $93M of equity income from companies Disney part-owns.
footerNote: Segment operating income: Entertainment $1,100M, Sports $191M, Experiences $3,309M (before corporate costs). Of the $2,484M of net income, $82M belongs to noncontrolling partners; $2,402M is attributable to Disney shareholders. The cost split (cost of services / cost of products) comes from Disney's Q1 FY26 10-Q; the earnings release reports the same totals.
